definition: Richard Stuart Sutton (born 1957 or 1958) is a Canadian computer scientist.
details: He is a professor of computing science at the University of Alberta and chief scientific advisor at the Alberta Machine Intelligence Institute. He co-founded in 2026 an AI startup, Oak Lab. Sutton is considered one of the founders of modern computational reinforcement learning. In particular, he contributed to temporal difference learning and policy gradient methods. He received the 2024 Turing Award with Andrew Barto.

explainer.lead: Richard S. Sutton is a Computer scientist. His work spans reinforcement learning, informatics, artificial intelligence and machine learning.

contributions.name: He proposed the "bitter lesson", an influential observation about AI scaling limits.
His doctoral dissertation introduced actor-critic architectures and temporal credit assignment.

He was influenced by Harry Klopf's work in the 1970s, which proposed that supervised learning is insufficient for AI or explaining intelligent behavior, and trial-and-error learning, driven by "hedonic aspects of behavior", is necessary.
Sutton introduced temporal-difference methods for prediction and control, establishing convergence properties and practical algorithms.
He proposed integrated learning and planning through the Dyna architecture.

timeline.what: Receives the Lifetime Achievement Award of the Canadian Artificial Intelligence Association
Named Fellow of the Royal Society
